semantic_correction.stem: A rural hospital without an on-site stroke neurologist activates its telestroke system for a client with suspected acute ischemic stroke. What is the main benefit of this system?

options.A: Provide rapid remote stroke expertise and imaging review to support acute treatment and transfer decisions.
options.B: Replace local nursing, emergency, and radiology care for the remainder of the hospitalization.
options.C: Delay acute treatment decisions until the client can be evaluated in person at a referral center.
options.D: Use remote consultation after reperfusion decisions are finished rather than during acute evaluation.

semantic_correction.rationale: The 2026 AHA/ASA acute ischemic stroke guideline states that telestroke bridges gaps in access to stroke expertise, particularly in remote hospitals without on-site neurological specialists. In acute care, telestroke and teleradiology support timely brain-imaging review, thrombolytic decision-making, and triage or transfer for endovascular thrombectomy when appropriate. Telestroke supplements local hands-on care rather than replacing it, and its value is greatest during the time-sensitive acute evaluation rather than after treatment decisions are complete.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Use telestroke to provide rapid remote stroke expertise, imaging-based treatment support, and transfer triage for hospitals without on-site stroke specialists.
semantic_correction.source_organization: American Heart Association / American Stroke Association (AHA/ASA)
semantic_correction.source_document_title: 2026 Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke
semantic_correction.source_version_date: Published January 26, 2026; current corrected guideline accessed August 21, 2026

semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: Telestroke provides remote specialist consultation and imaging-based decision support for suspected acute stroke, improving access to timely reperfusion and transfer decisions in hospitals lacking on-site stroke expertise.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: removed 'all'/'only' distractor cueing, shortened the correct answer, and centered the item on the guideline-supported telestroke functions of remote expertise, imaging review, acute treatment support, and transfer triage.

audit_findings_append.blueprint_locator: Management of Care — telehealth/interdisciplinary resources and transfer coordination
audit_findings_append.finding: The original answer was uniquely longest and distractors used absolutes. The revised item directly tests the main systems-of-care benefit of telestroke with balanced alternatives.

option_audit.A: Correct. It matches the guideline's description of telestroke as rapid remote expertise supporting imaging, treatment, and transfer decisions.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Telestroke supplements rather than replaces local bedside, emergency, and radiology care.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Telestroke is intended to reduce treatment delay in hospitals without local stroke expertise.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Acute reperfusion decision support is a central telestroke function, not a post-decision use only.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone captures the time-sensitive remote expertise and systems-of-care functions described in the 2026 guideline.
cueing_check: All four choices are descriptions of telestroke function of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.

checks: NCSBN 2026 Management of Care mapping confirmed
